cues.en: Welcome to this episode of the Common Sense Skeptic.
cues.zh: 欢迎收看这一期的《Common Sense Skeptic》。

cues.en: Earlier this month, Elon Musk was declared to be the richest man in the world, and his fanboys celebrated this questionable achievement by shoveling even more of their hard earned cash into Tesla's inflated stock price.
cues.zh: 本月早些时候，埃隆·马斯克被宣布为世界首富。他的粉丝们欢庆这一可疑的成就，又把更多辛苦赚来的钱砸进了特斯拉虚高的股价里。

cues.en: So what better way for us to kick off the new year than to demonstrate how Musk accumulated his reported massive wealth and how Musk is probably the least worthy individual to ever hold such an honor. But first, we're gonna start off this episode with a bit of an origin story of our own, and the reason why the Common Sense Skeptic Channel came to be.
cues.zh: 新年伊始，还有什么比揭示马斯克如何积累起据称的巨额财富，以及他可能是最不配拥有这份殊荣的人，更适合我们的开场呢？不过在此之前，我们先讲讲自己的起源故事，以及《Common Sense Skeptic》频道创立的缘由。

cues.en: Our crew are all fans of technology who grew up on a steady diet of science fiction. We followed along ever since Buck Rogers and Battlestar Galactica, the original series, were putting out new episodes.
cues.zh: 我们团队都是科技迷，从小就泡在科幻作品里长大。早在《巴克·罗杰斯》和原版《太空堡垒卡拉狄加》还在连载播出时，我们就在追了。

cues.en: Back when five bucks bought popcorn and a $2.50 Tuesday admission ticket to Star Wars in the theaters.
cues.zh: 那时候，五块钱不仅能买份爆米花，还能买到一张《星球大战》周二两块五的影院特价票。

cues.en: Star Wars, Star Trek, even Star Blazers.
cues.zh: 《星球大战》、《星际迷航》，甚至是《宇宙战舰大和号》。

cues.en: So would it surprise you to learn that we used to be fans of Elon Musk?
cues.zh: 所以，如果我说我们曾经也是 Elon Musk 的粉丝，你会觉得意外吗？

cues.en: It's true. Spotting him in Iron Man two where the Big Bang Theory was kinda cool back in the day, and the media made sure we knew who he was and all the technological marvels he had single handedly brought into the world.
cues.zh: 没错。当年在《钢铁侠2》里看到他和《生活大爆炸》联动还挺酷的，媒体也非要让我们知道他是谁，还有他单枪匹马带给世界的那些科技奇迹。

cues.en: PayPal,
cues.zh: PayPal，

cues.en: Tesla, SpaceX,
cues.zh: Tesla、SpaceX，

cues.en: all directly from the unparalleled brilliant mind of this single man who manifested his visions through sheer determination and grit. Who doesn't love a story like that? Right? Problem was, it was all a fiction we were being force fed. Fake news. We just didn't know it yet.
cues.zh: 全都直接出自这个人之手，他那无与伦比的聪明头脑，靠纯粹的决心和毅力把愿景变成了现实。谁不喜欢这样的故事呢？对吧？问题是，这一切都是硬灌给我们的虚构故事。假新闻。只是我们当时还不知道罢了。

cues.en: Around the same time Musk was pretending to be an actor, other stories were circulating online about new technologies that were going to reshape the world. Wonder products being fond over the media at the time included the water seer and thorium powered cars and condominiums hanging from orbiting asteroids that would float across the sky.
cues.zh: 大约在马斯克假装当演员的同时，网上也流传着其他故事，说新技术即将重塑世界。当时媒体大肆吹捧的神奇产品，包括能探测水源的仪器、钍动力汽车，还有挂在轨道小行星上、能飘过天空的公寓。

cues.en: All of which falling into the category of too good to be true, and alarm bells started ringing about these types of claims.
cues.zh: 这些故事都好得令人难以置信，人们开始对这类说法敲响警钟。

cues.en: Actually, one of the very first products that defined our belief was palcohol.
cues.zh: 其实，最早让我们坚定这种信念的产品之一就是 Palcohol。

cues.en: Remember that one? Powdered alcohol that you just added to water to make your favorite cocktails when you were out on a hike. The problem with that claim was alcohol is a solvent, not a solute,
cues.zh: 还记得那个吗？粉末状酒精，徒步时只要加点水，就能调出你最爱的鸡尾酒。但这种说法的破绽在于，酒精是溶剂，而不是溶质，

cues.en: which is impossible to dehydrate into a powder.
cues.zh: 根本不可能脱水做成粉末。

cues.en: Solar Freaking Roadways was next. Their CGI promotional videos declared their goal was to pave the roads of the world with solar tile panels that were impervious to damage, creating all the energy the world would ever need.
cues.zh: 接下来是 Solar Freaking Roadways。他们的 CGI 宣传片宣称，目标是用坚不可摧的太阳能地砖铺满全球道路，从而产生全世界所需的所有能源。

cues.en: Nonstop adulation and positive press washed over Scott and Julie Brousseau while they collected millions of dollars from Indiegogo
cues.zh: Scott和Julie Brousseau一边从Indiegogo众筹数百万美元，一边收获铺天盖地的吹捧和正面报道。

cues.en: and federal grants to produce this earth saving green tech.
cues.zh: 还拿到联邦拨款，用来打造这项拯救地球的绿色科技。

cues.en: But upon closer inspection,
cues.zh: 但仔细一查，

cues.en: none of their claims added up, especially the economics.
cues.zh: 他们的说法全都站不住脚，尤其是经济账。

cues.en: So we did what nobody else had done so far and broke down the numbers.
cues.zh: 于是我们做了此前没人做过的事，把数字拆开算了个清楚。

cues.en: Turned out the raw unassembled materials for solar roadways would add up to at least $205,000,000
cues.zh: 结果发现，太阳能公路的原材料（未组装）每英里四车道高速公路至少要花费2.05亿美元，

cues.en: per mile of four lane highway, and that was years ago.
cues.zh: 而且这还是多年前的数字。

cues.en: Despite all their awards and DOT grants and press coverage and announced projects,
cues.zh: 尽管它们拿过各种奖项、获得过交通部拨款、受到媒体报道，也宣布过不少项目，

cues.en: fifteen years after being founded, solar roadways has only ever amounted to little more than vaporware.
cues.zh: 太阳能道路公司成立十五年后，最终也只不过是个空头项目。

cues.en: At the time, Musk still flew under our radar despite his constant appearances on shows and news feeds and tech articles
cues.zh: 当时，尽管马斯克频频出现在节目、新闻动态和科技报道中，我们还是一直没太关注他，

cues.en: right up until the cave in Thailand flooded.
cues.zh: 直到泰国山洞遭遇洪水。

cues.en: Then he hit our wall.
cues.zh: 这时他撞上了我们的底线。

cues.en: As actual heroes were trying to save a dozen young soccer players and their coach from drowning in the cave,
cues.zh: 真正的英雄们正试图救出被困山洞、濒临溺水的十几名年轻足球队员和他们的教练，

cues.en: Musk decided this would be a great time for self promotion,
cues.zh: 马斯克却觉得这是个自我宣传的好时机，

cues.en: declaring he would provide a submarine to conduct a rescue.
cues.zh: 他声称自己会提供一艘潜艇参与救援。

cues.en: Vernon Unsworth, one of the lead rescue divers of this operation,
cues.zh: 作为本次救援的核心潜水员之一，Vernon Unsworth

cues.en: told the media and Musk, thanks but no thanks, that sub will be useless in this effort.
cues.zh: 对媒体和 Musk 表示，心领了但不必，那艘潜艇在这种救援中根本派不上用场。

cues.en: The fact was this pinch point in the tunnel was so tight that divers had to remove their air tanks and pull them alongside.
cues.zh: 事实上，通道中最狭窄的瓶颈处实在太窄了，潜水员必须卸下氧气瓶拖着走。

cues.en: This was so dangerous that an experienced Thai Navy SEAL named Samangunan
cues.zh: 这里的危险程度极高，以至于一名经验丰富的泰国海豹突击队员 Samangunan

cues.en: died while loading the tunnel with air tanks before the underwater extraction.
cues.zh: 在水下撤离行动前，进洞放置氧气瓶时不幸牺牲。

cues.en: Unsworth was absolutely correct in dismissing Musk's sub, which would never have gotten through that gap.
cues.zh: Unsworth 完全正确地驳回了 Musk 的潜艇方案，那东西根本不可能通过那个缝隙。

cues.en: Musk took that dismissal personally,
cues.zh: Musk 把这次驳回当成了针对自己，

cues.en: and that embarrassment led to Musk viciously attacking Unsworth on Twitter. The sheer stupidity Musk demonstrated during this attempted publicity stunt while there were young lives at stake was bad enough.
cues.zh: 而这种难堪导致 Musk 在 Twitter 上恶毒攻击 Unsworth。在这场公关作秀中，明明有年轻生命危在旦夕，Musk 表现出的愚蠢已经够糟糕了。

cues.en: But for him to do what he did to Vernon Unsworth on Twitter and in follow-up news articles tore the positive facade off of him permanently.
cues.zh: 但他在 Twitter 上以及后续新闻文章中对 Vernon Unsworth 所做的一切，彻底撕掉了他正面的伪装。

cues.en: Watching these events unfold, the question we kept asking ourselves was how could somebody so smart do something so stupid and so vile as this?
cues.zh: 看着这些事一件件发生，我们一直在问自己：一个这么聪明的人，怎么会做出如此愚蠢又卑劣的事？

cues.en: And the answer we came up with was,
cues.zh: 最后我们得出的答案是：

cues.en: maybe he's not that smart.
cues.zh: 也许他没那么聪明。

cues.en: Turns out that was an accurate conclusion. And the more research we do on Musk, the more solidified this conclusion becomes.
cues.zh: 事实证明，这个结论是准确的。我们对 Musk 研究得越多，这个结论就越牢固。

cues.en: Now that we've been able to nail down Musk's modus operandi, it's time to share what we've learned so that others can stop fawning over this megalomaniacal
cues.zh: 现在我们已经摸清了 Musk 的行事套路，是时候分享我们的发现了，这样其他人就能停止对这个自大狂

cues.en: imbecile that continues to fail upwards.
cues.zh: 蠢货的盲目崇拜了——他总能一路失败，却步步高升。

cues.en: We've all seen them. These memes that portray Elon Musk as a multifaceted genius solely responsible for these, quote, unquote, paradigm shifting companies.
cues.zh: 我们都见过这些梗图：它们把 Elon Musk 描绘成一个全能天才，凭一己之力撑起了这些所谓的“范式转移”公司。

cues.en: We've also seen the stories attached to this mythos about how he was a poor and abused child who turned himself into a self made billionaire.
cues.zh: 我们也听过围绕这个神话展开的故事，说他曾是一个穷困且遭受虐待的孩子，最终白手起家成为亿万富翁。

cues.en: It's time to put these claims to the test. Is he a self made billionaire?
cues.zh: 是时候检验一下这些说法了。他真的是白手起家的亿万富翁吗？

cues.en: And is he in fact the genius behind each of the companies he's credited with being the founder of?
cues.zh: 他真的就是那些挂着他“创始人”头衔的公司背后，真正的天才核心吗？

cues.en: So this is debunking Elon Musk. Our initial offering of 2021.
cues.zh: 所以这期我们来揭穿埃隆·马斯克。这是我们2021年的首期节目。

cues.en: Was born to May Haldeman and Errol Musk on 06/28/1971
cues.zh: 他于1971年6月28日出生，母亲是梅·霍尔德曼，父亲是埃罗尔·马斯克。

cues.en: in Pretoria South Africa. This fittingly makes him a Cancer. His mother May was 21, two years younger than her husband Errol, whom she would divorce only nine years later. As it turns out, the South African businessman who relentlessly pursued this beautiful aspiring model for seven years until she finally agreed to marry him, started physically abusing her pretty much as soon as they got married. After having three children together, May moved back to Canada to pursue her modeling career, and at 69 became the face of CoverGirl. Around the same time May became the face of CoverGirl, her 72 year old ex husband fathered a child with his own 30 year old stepdaughter from his second ex marriage. Which really isn't Elon's story, except Elon would bring similar misogynist attitudes into all of his future ex marriages.
cues.zh: 出生地是南非比勒陀利亚。这恰好让他成了巨蟹座。母亲梅当时21岁，比丈夫埃罗尔小两岁，而她在仅仅九年后就与他离婚了。原来，这位南非商人曾执着追求这位美丽的准模特长达七年，直到她终于答应嫁给他，可婚后几乎立刻就对她实施了身体虐待。共同育有三个孩子后，梅搬回加拿大追求模特事业，并在69岁时成为CoverGirl的代言面孔。差不多在梅成为CoverGirl代言人的同一时期，她72岁的前夫与自己第二段婚姻中30岁的继女育有一子。这其实不算埃隆的故事，只不过埃隆会把类似的厌女态度带进他未来所有的前婚姻中。

cues.en: Elon Musk is often portrayed as a poor kid who pulled himself up by his bootstraps.
cues.zh: 埃隆·马斯克常被描绘成一个靠自己打拼出头的穷小子。

cues.en: Reality is both sides of the family came from money, as was bragged about in an interview where they said they had so much money when they were younger, they could hardly fit it all in the safe.
cues.zh: 事实是，他父母双方家里都很有钱。他们曾在采访中炫耀说，年轻时钱多得连保险箱都快装不下了。

cues.en: May's father, Joshua Norman Haldeman, developed national and international stature stature as a political economist, provincial and national professional leader in chiropractic medicine, and sportsman adventurer.
cues.zh: 梅的父亲约书亚·诺曼·霍尔德曼在政治经济学领域颇有名望，也是省级和全国性的脊椎按摩疗法行业领袖，同时还是一位热衷冒险的运动员。

cues.en: In 1950, Haldeman picked up and moved his family to South Africa to become an amateur archaeologist hunting for the lost city of the Kalahari.
cues.zh: 1950年，Haldeman举家迁往南非，成了一名业余考古学家，四处搜寻喀拉哈里沙漠的失落之城。

cues.en: Errol Musk's parents were also well off tracing his military father's South African roots back two hundred years. His mother came from a well-to-do English family and had an elite education.
cues.zh: Errol Musk的家境也十分优渥，他父亲是军人，家族在南非的渊源可以追溯到两百年前；他母亲则来自英国富裕家庭，接受过精英教育。

cues.en: For his part, Errol was himself a gifted engineer, earned massive wealth as an engineering consultant and real estate developer and emerald mine co owner. According to Elon's father, the family enjoyed a lavish lifestyle replete with yachts, ski vacations, and expensive computers.
cues.zh: 至于Errol本人，也是位极具天赋的工程师，作为工程顾问、房地产开发商和祖母绿矿的合伙人，他积累了巨额财富。据Elon的父亲说，他们一家当时生活极其奢华，游艇、滑雪度假和昂贵的电脑应有尽有。

cues.en: Musk himself enjoyed a privileged upbringing and education at private school, all of which Musk now denies.
cues.zh: 马斯克本人曾在私立学校接受优渥的教育，如今他却对此全盘否认。

cues.en: But not every teenage kid can walk into Tiffany's with loose emeralds in their pockets and walk out with $2,000.
cues.zh: 但不是每个十几岁的孩子都能兜里揣着散装祖母绿走进蒂芙尼，再带着两千美元出来。

cues.en: When his parents divorced and his mother moved back to Canada, Musk initially stayed with his dad in South Africa.
cues.zh: 父母离婚、母亲搬回加拿大后，马斯克起初留在南非和父亲一起生活。

cues.en: Musk moved to Canada at the age of 17 to live with his mom to avoid serving in the South African military.
cues.zh: 马斯克17岁时搬到加拿大和母亲一起住，以免在南非服兵役。

cues.en: Musk attended Queen's University on scholarships.
cues.zh: Musk 靠奖学金就读于 Queen's University。

cues.en: So how he racked up the 6 figure student debt that he whines about is anybody's guess. Maybe it's because he didn't graduate before moving to the University of Pennsylvania,
cues.zh: 所以他整天抱怨的那笔六位数学生贷款是怎么欠下的，谁也说不准。也许是因为他在转学到 University of Pennsylvania 之前根本没毕业，

cues.en: and he was so poor that he and another student named Adio Resi bought a 10 bedroom frat house that they used as their own personal illegal nightclub.
cues.zh: 而且他“穷”到和一个叫 Adio Resi 的学生合伙买下了一栋有10间卧室的兄弟会大宅，用来当他们私人的非法夜店。

cues.en: Resi recently posted a photo of the house, and it still stands.
cues.zh: Resi 最近还晒出了那栋房子的照片，现在它依然立在那儿。

cues.en: Musk is also often portrayed as a genius with an estimated IQ somewhere in the mid one fifties. Problem is, that hasn't actually been put to the test since he was in grade school. And when he comes up with a concept such as the Hyperloop white paper, which is not only tremendously flat at a basic physics level, it was also plagiarized from a 100 year old patent and a 200 year old concept,
cues.zh: 马斯克也常被描绘成天才，据估算，他的智商大约在 150 到 160 之间。问题是，自从上小学后，他就再也没有接受过智商测试。而他提出的概念，比如《超级高铁》白皮书，从基础物理学角度看就极其肤浅，还抄袭了一个百年前的专利和一个两百年前的构想，

cues.en: one has to wonder about his mental competency.
cues.zh: 这不免让人怀疑他的心智能力。

cues.en: Anyone thinking that a turbine is going to pull you through an airless environment while that vehicle is being held off the ground using compressed air in a vacuum is fundamentally scientifically
cues.zh: 谁要是觉得，在真空环境下靠涡轮能拉着车跑，同时还能靠压缩空气让车悬浮起来，那他在科学常识上基本就是

cues.en: clueless and needs to check out the episodes Thunderfoot has done on this topic immediately.
cues.zh: 一无所知，真得赶紧去看看 Thunderfoot 针对这个话题做的几期视频。

cues.en: Then, of course, after Musk has an idea people are fawning over, he has to immediately lie to his followers to create additional hype, such as this fake news about getting approval for a New York to DC hyperloop or this one about building one from San Francisco to LA.
cues.zh: 当然了，每当 Musk 抛出一个让人狂热追捧的想法后，他就会立刻向粉丝撒谎来制造更多噱头，比如吹嘘纽约到华盛顿的 Hyperloop 已经获批这种假新闻，或者说要修一条从旧金山到洛杉矶的线路。

cues.en: Add to this nonsense the concept of underground freeways accessed by elevators using electric skates, or the absolute insanity of drilling computer interfaces into your brain to play video games. And even W. C. Fields would have to wonder, is he dazzling you with brilliance or baffling you with bullshit?
cues.zh: 再加上地下高速公路的荒唐构想：人们坐电梯下去，再踩着电动滑板通行；还有把电脑接口钻进大脑、用来玩电子游戏这种彻头彻尾的疯狂想法。就连 W. C. 菲尔兹也得琢磨：他是在用才华让你眼花缭乱，还是在用胡扯把你绕晕？

cues.en: Judging from the ridiculous claims Musk is making about the terraforming and colonization of Mars, we have to believe it's the latter. And for anyone arguing Musk has a PhD to back up the genius claim, here are those facts. Musk was accepted into Stanford in California for PhD studies.
cues.zh: 从马斯克关于火星改造和殖民的那些荒唐说法来看，我们只能相信是后者。至于有人说马斯克有博士学位，足以证明他是天才，事实是这样的：马斯克被加州的斯坦福大学录取，攻读博士学位。

cues.en: But he dropped out after only two days to pursue his first business enterprise with his brother. And that's where this story actually starts.
cues.zh: 但他仅待了两天就退学了，和哥哥一起开始了他的第一次创业。而我们的故事也正是从这里真正开始的。

cues.en: Instead of going to Stanford, Musk and his brother Kimball decided to create an online directory akin to the yellow pages to take advantage of the early stages of the Internet boom. To that end, in 1995,
cues.zh: Musk 和他的哥哥 Kimball 没有选择留在 Stanford，而是决定顺应早期互联网浪潮，做一个类似于黄页的在线名录。为此，在 1995 年，

cues.en: they formed a global information network, would later become Zip two, whose goal it was to convince businesses to form an online presence and directory.
cues.zh: 他们成立了一家名为 Global Information Network 的公司，也就是后来的 Zip2，其目标是说服企业建立线上业务并加入他们的名录。

cues.en: The stories that Musk tells about these early years living in the office and whatnot seem to be mostly for dramatic effect since their rich father gave them $28,000
cues.zh: 马斯克讲的这些早年在办公室打地铺之类的故事，多半是为了营造戏剧效果，因为他们有钱的父亲给了他们两万八千美元

cues.en: towards getting this venture going at a time when a minimum wage in California
cues.zh: 来启动这家公司，而当时加州的最低工资

cues.en: Musk may be on record now as saying he hates his father, but he apparently didn't hate him enough to turn down daddy's money or his mother's as it turns out. According to May's memoirs, she visited the boys every six weeks from Eastern Canada, buying groceries and furniture and giving them another $10,000 to keep the lights on. Man, it must suck being so hard done by.
cues.zh: 马斯克现在或许公开说过他恨父亲，但显然还没恨到拒绝老爸的钱的地步，结果连老妈的钱也照收。根据梅耶的回忆录，她每六周从加拿大东部来看望两个儿子一次，买食品杂货和家具，还又给了他们一万美元来维持开销。哎，日子过得这么“艰难”可真够惨的。

cues.en: Enter Greg Currie, a Canadian family friend through the father that claims to hate. Currie was a Canadian real estate developer with business ties and connections that the brothers did not have, so Currie came in as a co founder and mentor for the boys. Currie's roles in the company were those of investor, bringing another $8,000 of much needed cash, as well as VP of business development,
cues.zh: 格雷格·柯里登场了，他是通过那个声称憎恨的父亲结识的加拿大家庭朋友。柯里是一位加拿大房地产开发商，拥有兄弟们所没有的商业关系和人脉，因此柯里作为联合创始人和导师加入了进来。柯里在公司中的角色是投资者，带来了另外8000美元急需的现金，以及业务发展副总裁，

cues.en: and as it turns out, referee of literal fist fights between Elon and Kimball in the office.
cues.zh: 而事实证明，他还是埃隆和金博尔在办公室里真实拳脚相向时的裁判。

cues.en: It was Curry's connections that brought the venture capitalists to the table, not these squabbling siblings.
cues.zh: 把风险投资人拉到谈判桌前的，是Curry的人脉，而不是这些争吵不休的兄弟。

cues.en: Once the VC money came pouring in through Greg, the highest office Musk held in the company was that of chief technology officer or CTO.
cues.zh: Greg带来的风投资金涌入后，Musk在公司担任的最高职位只是首席技术官，也就是CTO。

cues.en: Due to Elon's inability to deal with people, he was not even considered for the CEO position that was filled by Rich Sorkin.
cues.zh: 由于Elon不擅长与人打交道，他连CEO的职位都没被考虑，该职位由Rich Sorkin出任。

cues.en: Prior to joining Zip2 as the chairman and CEO, Sorkin was a senior product manager for Pocket Computers, director of emerging tech at Phoenix Technologies,
cues.zh: 在加入Zip2担任董事长兼CEO之前，Sorkin曾是Pocket Computers的高级产品经理、Phoenix Technologies新兴技术总监，

cues.en: and VP general manager of Creative Technology Limited, where he oversaw an eightfold increase in revenue over three years to $800,000,000
cues.zh: 以及Creative Technology Limited的副总裁兼总经理，在那里他负责的业务三年内收入增长了八倍，达到8亿美元

cues.en: annually.
cues.zh: 的年收入。

cues.en: Sorkin's previous resume and education and his circle of influence dwarfed anything Musk brought to the table. Unlike Musk, Sorkin did graduate from Stanford in 1988 with his MBA
cues.zh: 相比之下，Sorkin 之前的履历、学历以及人脉圈，完全让 Musk 相形见绌。与 Musk 不同，Sorkin 确实在 1988 年拿到了斯坦福的 MBA 学位，

cues.en: after graduating from Yale with a Bachelor of Science in Economics.
cues.zh: 在此之前，他还获得了耶鲁大学的经济学理科学士学位。

cues.en: Elon was given the position of CTO. However, the code Musk wrote, as it turned out, was poorly written, difficult to update, and impossible to expand.
cues.zh: Elon 当时被任命为 CTO。然而事实证明，Musk 写的代码质量很差，既难以维护，又根本无法扩展。

cues.en: So in 1996,
cues.zh: 所以在 1996 年，

cues.en: Sorkin hired professional coders to completely scrap what Musk had done, eventually rewriting every line of code in the platform. So, essentially, Musk contributed nothing to the end product that Curie would use to attract additional investment money.
cues.zh: Sorkin 聘请了专业程序员彻底废弃了 Musk 的代码，最终把平台的每一行代码都重写了一遍。因此本质上，对于 Curie 用来吸引后续投资的最终产品，Musk 几乎没有任何代码贡献。

cues.en: Musk, upset that his work was being dismantled, demanded that these new professional coders work these same insane hours that he did, but they were only willing to commit to nine to five while rewriting this electronic version of the yellow pages. In making these demands, Musk earned the reputation for being quite unreasonable to work for.
cues.zh: Musk对于自己的工作被拆解感到不满，要求这些新的专业程序员像他一样疯狂加班，但他们只愿意朝九晚五地重写这本电子版黄页。由于这些要求，Musk落得了相当不讲理的上司名声。

cues.en: In April 1998, Sorkin made a deal with CitySearch to merge in a $300,000,000
cues.zh: 1998年4月，Sorkin与CitySearch达成协议，以3亿美元的

cues.en: deal that would have seen Sorkin become the new CEO of the combined companies.
cues.zh: 交易进行合并，这笔交易本会让Sorkin成为合并后公司的新CEO。

cues.en: Musk originally greenlit the deal, but then kiboshed it by leading a revolt against Sorkin, causing Zip2 to fall into such disarray that Derek Proutian, a venture capitalist board member at Zip2 and three times Stanford Grad, had to step up and take control of the company as CEO.
cues.zh: Musk 最初同意了这笔交易，但随后带头反对 Sorkin 从而叫停了它，导致 Zip2 陷入一片混乱，Zip2 的风投董事、斯坦福三料毕业生 Derek Proudian 不得不出面接管公司担任 CEO。

cues.en: He immediately started looking for a buyer for this growing dumpster fire.
cues.zh: 他立刻开始为这个愈演愈烈的烂摊子寻找买家。

cues.en: In February 1999, despite constantly losing money,
cues.zh: 1999 年 2 月，尽管公司一直在亏钱，

cues.en: Compaq offered Pradyen $305,000,000
cues.zh: Compaq 还是向 Proudian 开出了 3.05 亿美元的报价，

cues.en: to the company, lock, stock, and barrel. This deal went through, and Zip2 was absorbed into Compaq's AltaVista platform.
cues.zh: 全盘收购了这家公司。交易最终达成，Zip2 被并入了 Compaq 的 AltaVista 平台。

cues.en: Those of us who lived through the nineties remember the .com tech boom followed by the bubble and burst.
cues.zh: 经历过90年代的人都记得当年的互联网热潮，以及随之而来的泡沫破裂。

cues.en: This transaction definitely falls into that category.
cues.zh: 这笔交易绝对也属于那一类。

cues.en: Here is another parallel from that same time frame. Most of you know who Kevin O'Leary is, the self proclaimed Mr. Wonderful from Shark Tank and Dragon's Den fame.
cues.zh: 同一时期还有个类似的例子。你们大多数人都知道 Kevin O'Leary 是谁，就是《Shark Tank》和《Dragon's Den》里自封为“奇迹先生”的那位。

cues.en: O'Leary's biggest claim to fame is that in May 1999, Mattel paid $3,800,000,000
cues.zh: O'Leary 最出名的事迹，是在1999年5月让 Mattel 斥资38亿美元，

cues.en: for Kevin O'Leary's The Learning Company software company to form Mattel Interactive. Turned out, O'Leary's cooked books and outdated assets were pretty much worthless, and they were almost literally given away to the Gore's technology group for 27,000,000 less than a year later.
cues.zh: 收购了他旗下的 The Learning Company 软件公司并组建了 Mattel Interactive。结果证明，O'Leary 做了假账，那些过时的资产几乎一文不值，不到一年后，它们就以2700万美元的白菜价甩卖给了 Gores Technology Group。

cues.en: In the time Mattel held on to TLC,
cues.zh: 在美泰持有 TLC 的这段时间里，

cues.en: they encountered losses in the hundreds of millions of dollars. Investors watched their share price plummet from $26.44 in March '99 to $8.94 a year later. Mattel had to lay off 10% of their workforce to eke their way back to profitability.
cues.zh: 他们遭遇了数亿美元的亏损。投资者眼睁睁看着股价从 99 年 3 月的 26.44 美元，一路暴跌到一年后的 8.94 美元。美泰不得不裁员 10%，才勉强扭亏为盈。

cues.en: But the producers of Shark Tank conveniently leave out all those details from the opening credits of the show to let you believe that Kevin O'Leary is some sort of next level business billionaire guru.
cues.zh: 但《Shark Tank》的制片人却巧妙地在片头隐去了所有这些细节，好让你以为 Kevin O'Leary 是什么神级商业亿万富翁。

cues.en: Sound familiar?
cues.zh: 听起来耳熟吗？

cues.en: Right around the same time O'Leary single handedly killed off the educational software market, the Zip2 deal went through, and Compaq suffered for it.
cues.zh: 就在 O'Leary 一手毁掉教育软件市场的同一时期，Zip2 的交易达成了，而 Compaq 为此付出了沉重代价。

cues.en: Their strategy of buying assets at ridiculous premiums rather than develop them in house at wholesale
cues.zh: 他们不去低成本自主研发，而是以离谱的溢价四处收购资产，这种策略

cues.en: caused the once prominent computer company to flounder. In January 1999, Compaq's stock hit an all time high of $47.62
cues.zh: 导致这家曾经赫赫有名的计算机公司陷入困境。1999 年 1 月，Compaq 的股价创下了 47.62 美元的历史新高

cues.en: a share. This transaction completed in February.
cues.zh: 每股。这笔交易在 2 月份完成。

cues.en: By April, the stock had dropped to half its value to $24.25.
cues.zh: 到4月份，股价腰斩，跌到了24.25美元。

cues.en: And from there, it was a steady slide to when they were taken over by HP in September 2001 with a closing stock price on the transaction date of $12.35.
cues.zh: 从那之后便是一路下滑，直到2001年9月被HP收购，交易日的收盘价仅为12.35美元。

cues.en: Anyone who bought and held CPQ at its height lost 75% of their investment by the time it was converted into HP stock.
cues.zh: 任何在最高点买入并持有CPQ的人，等换成HP股票时，投资都已经亏损了75%。

cues.en: If you lost money on CPQ,
cues.zh: 如果你在CPQ上亏了钱，

cues.en: the Zip2 deal definitely played a role in that loss.
cues.zh: Zip2这笔交易绝对是难辞其咎。

cues.en: At the end of the day, Zip2 never managed to create a single penny in profit for Compaq from acquisition to abortion.
cues.zh: 到头来，Zip2 从被收购到最终被砍，都没能给 Compaq 赚到哪怕一分钱利润。

cues.en: But none of that mattered to the Musk brothers or Takuri who all made out like bandits.
cues.zh: 但这丝毫影响不到 Musk 兄弟和 Takuri，他们个个都赚得盆满钵满。

cues.en: Elon netted $22,000,000.
cues.zh: Elon 到手 2200 万美元。

cues.en: Kimball only got $15,000,000.
cues.zh: Kimbal 也有 1500 万美元。

cues.en: Curry, who was the Zip2 business developer and co founder, made enough money to invest in Elon's next venture, but he played no role in the company.
cues.zh: 作为 Zip2 业务拓展兼联合创始人的 Curry，赚的钱也足够投资 Elon 的下一个项目，但他并没有在该公司任职。

cues.en: Curry in 2012 at the age of 51 of a heart attack in New York City.
cues.zh: Curry于2012年在纽约市因心脏病发作去世，享年51岁。

cues.en: After Musk cashed in with Zip two, he immediately took $1,000,000 of his windfall and bought a McLaren f one supercar to show off to his his circle of friends and his girlfriend at the time, which made international headline news.
cues.zh: Musk通过Zip2套现后，立刻拿出100万美元的意外之财买了一辆McLaren F1超级跑车，向朋友圈和当时的女友炫耀，这成了国际头条新闻。

cues.en: This purchase is the perfect analogy for Musk to be sure. Just like the company he sold, he didn't know how to pilot it or keep it on the road, and the poor vehicle suffered dearly at his hands before he wrote the uninsured car off, showing off for a man by the name of Peter Thiel, a name we will hear again very shortly.
cues.zh: 这次购买对Musk来说是个完美的类比。就像他卖掉的公司一样，他不知道如何驾驶它或让它保持在路上，这辆可怜的车在他手里遭受了重创，最后他在一个叫Peter Thiel的人面前炫耀时把没上保险的车撞毁了，这个名字我们很快就会再次听到。

cues.en: Following
cues.zh: 随后

cues.en: the windfall sale of Zip two to Compaq, Musk turned his remaining money and focus to his next venture he called x.com.
cues.zh: 把Zip2高价卖给康柏后，马斯克把剩下的钱和精力投入到他称之为x.com的下一个创业项目。

cues.en: Of course, everyone knows the story of how Musk single handedly set out to revolutionize the banking industry, except you don't see the name Harris Fricker anywhere. And he was kind of important to that company, not only as a banking expert, but also as a cofounder.
cues.zh: 当然，大家都知道马斯克单枪匹马要颠覆银行业的故事，只是你到处都看不到哈里斯·弗里克这个名字。而他对那家公司还挺重要的，不仅作为银行专家，还作为联合创始人。

cues.en: So was Ed Ho, a former Zip2 executive, and so was Christopher Payne, Harris Fricker's friend and colleague in the banking industry, who has apparently never ever been photographed. Ed Ho, on the other hand, has only ever had one picture taken of him. Seriously, those are the only pictures we could find.
cues.zh: 埃德·何也是如此，他是Zip2的前高管，克里斯托弗·佩恩也是，他是哈里斯·弗里克在银行业的朋友和同事，而后者显然从未被拍过照片。另一方面，埃德·何只被拍过一张照片。说真的，这些就是我们能找到的全部照片了。

cues.en: Judging from the differences between the English and the Spanish versions of Wikipedia,
cues.zh: 从维基百科英文版和西班牙语版的差异来看，

cues.en: someone has been rewriting x.com's
cues.zh: 有人一直在改写 x.com 的

cues.en: history. Compare these screenshots for x.com from both sites, and you'll find the English version has been redacted to remove mention of everybody but Musk at x dot com, but the Spanish version still names the three other men, their cofounderships,
cues.zh: 历史。对比两个网站上的 x.com 截图，你会发现英文版已经删掉了所有人的名字，只留下 x.com 的马斯克；而西班牙语版仍提到了另外三位男性、他们的联合创始人身份，

cues.en: and their departure trajectories.
cues.zh: 以及他们各自离开的经过。

cues.en: Of these three men, it was Fricker who played the most important role in this new start up. Fricker is a banker with a bachelor's from Saint Francis Xavier and a Rhodes Scholar's master from Oxford University to back it up. He was the banking master x.com needed to make this happen, and he brought the people he needed with him. Musk met Fricker during his internship at Bank of Nova Scotia, and convinced Fricker to come on board in November 1999 to help found the company. When x.com was formed, Musk ruled the rest of his Zip2 windfall into x.com,
cues.zh: 在这三人中，Fricker 在这家新创公司成立之初发挥了最重要的作用。他是一名银行家，拥有圣弗朗西斯泽维尔大学的学士学位，以及牛津大学罗德奖学金硕士学位。他正是 x.com 为实现目标所需要的银行业专家，也带来了所需的人才。Musk 在加拿大丰业银行实习期间认识了 Fricker，并在 1999 年 11 月说服他加入，共同创办公司。x.com 成立时，Musk 把 Zip2 剩余的收益全部投入 x.com，

cues.en: making sure with his larger investment that he would retain control of the company by assigning himself as chairman.
cues.zh: 并通过追加投资确保自己掌控公司，同时任命自己为董事长。

cues.en: Musk brought on Bill Harris as CEO, who brought his experience as CEO at Intuit Inc with him. Which didn't sit well with Fricker, who had moved from Canada to Silicon Valley to start this company and make his mark. Despite an initial rapport as friends, Musk and Fricker rarely saw eye to eye in business. Fricker simply wanted to create an online bank, but Musk kept insisting their company had to revolutionize the banking industry.
cues.zh: Musk请来Bill Harris担任CEO，后者带来了他在Intuit Inc担任CEO的经验。这让Fricker很不满，他可是从加拿大搬到硅谷来创办这家公司、想闯出一番名堂的。尽管两人起初作为朋友颇为投缘，但在业务上Musk和Fricker几乎从不意见一致。Fricker只想创办一家网上银行，但Musk一直坚持他们的公司必须彻底变革银行业。

cues.en: Fricker accurately accused Musk of overhyping their product, and tensions got so bad that Fricker attempted a boardroom coup against Musk and Bill Harris to take the CEO positions five months after founding the company together.
cues.zh: Fricker 准确指出马斯克过度吹嘘了他们的产品。两人关系恶化到如此地步：共同创办公司仅五个月后，Fricker 就试图在董事会发动政变，夺走马斯克和比尔·哈里斯的 CEO 职位。

cues.en: When that was unsuccessful,
cues.zh: 这次行动失败后，

cues.en: Fricker, Payne, and Ho all simply left and they took all the best software engineers with them, leaving behind Musk and whatever staff remained in May 2000 with a disheveled shell of a barely functional platform.
cues.zh: Fricker、Payne 和 Ho 全都离开了，还带走了最优秀的软件工程师。2000 年 5 月，马斯克和留下的员工只能面对一个乱成一团、勉强能运行的平台空壳。

cues.en: Scott Anderson, a software engineer who started working at x.com on 08/01/1999,
cues.zh: Scott Anderson，一名软件工程师，于1999年8月1日开始在x.com工作，

cues.en: described the fallout as complete insanity,
cues.zh: 将这场余波形容为彻底的疯狂，

cues.en: describing their software as a Hollywood movie set of a website that barely fooled the venture capitalists.
cues.zh: 称他们的软件就像一个好莱坞电影布景般的网站，勉强骗过了风险投资人。

cues.en: Was apparently so pissed off with Musk on his departure, he doesn't even bother mentioning x.com
cues.zh: 据说他在离职时对Musk极为不满，甚至根本不屑提及x.com

cues.en: whatsoever,
cues.zh: 任何相关内容，

cues.en: despite setting the company up using his experience, connections, and education in the banking
cues.zh: 尽管他是凭借自己在银行业的经验、人脉和教育背景创办了这家公司

cues.en: Frigar recently retired as the CEO for stifled GMP Capital, lasting twelve years in the organization he joined shortly after parting ways with Musk. The other original founders also went on to have their own successes without having to deal any longer with Musk. None of them mentioned their association with x.com on their professional profiles whatsoever.
cues.zh: Frigar最近从GMP Capital的CEO职位上退休，他在与Musk分道扬镳后不久加入该公司，在那里待了十二年。其他几位原始创始人也各自取得了成功，无需再与Musk打交道。他们中没有人在自己的职业履历上提及与x.com的关联。

cues.en: After Fricker left and took his friends with him, Musk desperately needed money, and he was able to sweet talk Mike Moritz of Sequoia Capital into investing in their platform, which was barely functional now. But Moritz didn't see through this sham, and he threw money at it anyway.
cues.zh: Fricker 离开并带走了他的朋友们后，Musk 急需资金，于是靠着一番甜言蜜语，说服 Sequoia Capital 的 Mike Moritz 投资他们的平台。那时的平台几乎已经无法正常运行了。但 Moritz 没看穿这场骗局，还是把钱投了进去。

cues.en: Meanwhile, another company was making their mark in the online finance world, and this one didn't have all this inner turmoil,
cues.zh: 与此同时，另一家公司正在在线金融领域崭露头角，而且这家公司没有这些内部纷争，

cues.en: at least not yet.
cues.zh: 至少当时还没有。

cues.en: A similar banking concept created by Peter Thiel and Max Levchin at a startup called Confinity
cues.zh: 彼得·蒂尔和马克斯·列夫钦在一家名为 Confinity 的初创公司里开发了类似的银行业务概念

cues.en: was gaining notoriety with their payment platform called PayPal,
cues.zh: 他们的支付平台 PayPal 正逐渐声名鹊起，

cues.en: which was developed through 1998
cues.zh: 这个平台于 1998 年开发

cues.en: and released in July 1999,
cues.zh: 并于 1999 年 7 月发布，

cues.en: almost a year before Musk and Harris had their falling out over at x.com.
cues.zh: 那时距离马斯克和哈里斯在 x.com 因分歧闹翻，差不多还有一年。

cues.en: So right off the bat, three things to note here. Number one, Musk did not found the company that wrote PayPal in December 1998.
cues.zh: 先说三点。第一，马斯克并不是 1998 年 12 月创立了开发 PayPal 的那家公司。

cues.en: Number two, Musk did not write PayPal.
cues.zh: 第二，Musk 并没有编写 PayPal 的代码。

cues.en: And number three, the company was not even called PayPal.
cues.zh: 第三，那家公司当时甚至都不叫 PayPal。

cues.en: So when Musk is introduced as the founder of PayPal, there's just so much wrong with that statement. If it wasn't pathetic, it might even be funny.
cues.zh: 所以当 Musk 被介绍为 PayPal 的创始人时，这种说法错漏百出。要不是显得有些可悲，甚至还挺搞笑的。

cues.en: Musk was watching the Confinity platform take off, so Musk started copying their promotional model.
cues.zh: Musk 眼看着 Confinity 平台迅速崛起，于是便开始照搬他们的推广模式。

cues.en: Luke Nosek's primary campaign for Confinity that Musk copied was offering cash incentives for new clients and client referrals,
cues.zh: Musk 抄袭的主要是 Luke Nosek 为 Confinity 设计的活动，即为新用户注册和邀请好友提供现金奖励，

cues.en: which drove both companies into the red ink. TL and company eventually decided if you can't beat them, eat them. So Confinity bought or merged with x.com
cues.zh: 这导致两家公司都陷入了巨额亏损。Thiel 和他的团队最终决定，打不过就吞并他们。于是 Confinity 收购或与 x.com 合并，

cues.en: in the March 2000 under Bill Harris who would remain as CEO of the merged companies. By virtue of his shares value, Musk became chairman, and became the chief financial officer. Combining the companies was a nightmare, each having their own corporate culture, and the two were like oil and water. Harris and Thiel particularly didn't see eye to eye on how to handle the combined company which was sinking deeper into debt in large part because the site was being constantly hacked by thieves.
cues.zh: 这发生在 2000 年 3 月，Bill Harris 继续担任合并后公司的 CEO。凭借持股价值，Musk 成了董事长，（Thiel）则出任首席财务官。两家公司的合并堪称一场噩梦，各自的企业文化水火不容。Harris 和 Thiel 在如何管理这家合并后的公司上尤其意见不合，而由于网站不断遭到黑客窃贼的攻击，公司在很大程度上正陷于越来越深的债务泥潭。

cues.en: This discord led Thiel to quit the company. Musk arranged an emergency board meeting to seize the CEO position away from Harris, and that was a move that brought Thiel back as chairman in April 2000.
cues.zh: 这场不和导致 Thiel 离开了公司。Musk 随即安排了一次紧急董事会，把 Harris 赶下了 CEO 的位置，并在 2000 年 4 月借此将 Thiel 请回并担任董事长。

cues.en: In his new position as CEO, Musk wanted to phase out all other names in favor of his beloved x.com.
cues.zh: 升任 CEO 后，Musk 想要逐步淘汰所有其他名字，只保留他钟爱的 x.com。

cues.en: Problem was focus groups hated x.com
cues.zh: 可问题是，焦点小组的用户非常讨厌 x.com，

cues.en: since it sounded like a porn site. This caused a rift in the former Confinity ranks, which in turn angered Musk, who loved the name.
cues.zh: 因为这听起来像个色情网站。这在前 Confinity 员工内部引发了分歧，同时也惹恼了极度喜欢这个名字的 Musk。

cues.en: Despite bleeding red ink, the company became popular as an online means to transfer funds. But with that popularity came increased fraud as hackers discovered they could easily access financial data on the site to siphon funds.
cues.zh: 尽管持续严重亏损，该公司作为一种在线转账方式还是迅速风靡起来。但随之而来的却是日益猖獗的欺诈行为，黑客发现他们可以轻易获取网站上的财务数据来窃取资金。

cues.en: Additionally, bank fees from the increasing transactions started adding up very quickly. It was obvious now that the company lacked a solid business structure as well as a way to offset the money it was losing, and they had no plan to combat the fraud it suffered.
cues.zh: 此外，交易量激增带来的银行手续费也开始迅速堆积。很显然，公司当时既缺乏稳固的商业架构，也没办法弥补持续的亏损，更没有任何应对诈骗的方案。

cues.en: Chief financial officer Roloff Bota, now a partner at Sequoia Capital, suspected Musk as the new CEO was not presenting his board with accurate assessments of the company's issues.
cues.zh: 时任首席财务官、现为 Sequoia Capital 合伙人的 Roloff Bota 怀疑，作为新任 CEO 的 Musk 并没有向董事会如实汇报公司面临的问题。

cues.en: And enough people started questioning Musk's decisions that they formed a coalition of former x.com and Confinity board members with the intent to dethrone Musk. Six months after Musk deposed Bill Harris as CEO, Musk himself became the target. And this coalition voted Musk be removed from the CEO position while Elon was flying to Sydney, Australia for his honeymoon with his first ex wife Justine, who was the eventual mother of six of his children.
cues.zh: 随着质疑 Musk 决策的人越来越多，前 x.com 和 Confinity 的董事会成员联手组成了联盟，意图罢免 Musk；就在 Musk 把 Bill Harris 赶下 CEO 职位仅仅六个月后，他自己也成了被清洗的目标；趁着 Elon 和第一任妻子 Justine（后来为他生了六个孩子）正飞往澳大利亚悉尼度蜜月时，这个联盟投票通过了罢免他 CEO 职位的决定。

cues.en: Justine gave Marie Claire quite the interview about her time with Musk, the way she was treated, and how Musk left his family behind for a British starlet named Tallulah Riley, who he would later divorce not once, but twice.
cues.zh: Justine 接受了《Marie Claire》的一次深度采访，谈到她和 Musk 相处的经历、自己受到的对待，以及 Musk 如何抛下家人，转而追求名叫 Tallulah Riley 的英国年轻女演员，后来还和她离了两次婚。

cues.en: The linchpin to this coup was Peter Thiel returning as CEO, which he agreed to do. Musk found out he had been fired as CEO when he landed on Australia and immediately headed back on the first available flight to plead his case, but nobody was interested in hearing it. Musk was removed as CEO on 09/24/2000.
cues.zh: 这场夺权的关键是 Peter Thiel 同意回来担任 CEO。Musk 飞抵澳大利亚时才得知自己已被免去 CEO 一职，随即搭乘最早的航班赶回去为自己辩护，但没人愿意听。他于 2000 年 9 月 24 日被免去 CEO 职务。

cues.en: He was formally terminated from the company on 03/09/2001.
cues.zh: 2001年3月9日，他被公司正式解雇。

cues.en: That full separation agreement can be found on corporate.finelaw.com.
cues.zh: 完整的离职协议可以在 corporate.finelaw.com 上找到。

cues.en: And it has some very interesting language woven into page three paragraph five regarding the deletion of reference to founders on the PayPal website,
cues.zh: 协议的第三页第五段有一些非常耐人寻味的措辞，涉及删除 PayPal 网站上有关创始人的表述，

cues.en: which would allow Musk to inaccurately in the future call him a founder of the company.
cues.zh: 这就让马斯克日后可以错误地称自己是公司的创始人。

cues.en: After Musk was terminated from all roles in the company, Thio rebranded the company to PayPal and removed all trace of the x.com branding. He took the company public in February 2002 with an IPO valued at $800,000,000
cues.zh: 在马斯克被解除公司所有职务后，蒂尔将公司更名为 PayPal，并清除了 x.com 品牌的所有痕迹。2002年2月，他带领公司上市，IPO 估值达8亿美元，

cues.en: before eBay bought the shop Lock, Stock and Barrel for $1,500,000,000
cues.zh: 随后 eBay 以15亿美元整体收购了这家公司，

cues.en: October of the same year. So as it turns out, not only did Musk not found PayPal,
cues.zh: 就在同年10月。所以事实证明，马斯克不仅没有创立 PayPal，

cues.en: he never even worked for a company called PayPal.
cues.zh: 他压根没在PayPal这家公司工作过。

cues.en: He had nothing to do with the renaming of the company, PayPal's IPO, or the subsequent sale to eBay that made Musk rich by accident.
cues.zh: 他跟公司改名、PayPal的IPO，以及后来卖给eBay都毫无关系——马斯克是碰巧因此发了财。

cues.en: From this windfall that Musk received thanks to Peter Thiel's efforts, Musk took the $180,000,000
cues.zh: 马斯克靠着Peter Thiel的努力得到这笔意外之财后，拿出他收到的那1.8亿美元，

cues.en: he received and sunk portions into Tesla, SpaceX,
cues.zh: 分别投了一部分到Tesla、SpaceX，

cues.en: and Solar City.
cues.zh: 还有Solar City。

cues.en: We're gonna take a break right now so you can get up and have a stretch, grab a drink, and then join us when you're ready to click part two of this presentation.
cues.zh: 我们现在休息一下，大家可以站起来伸个懒腰、喝点东西，准备好了就回来点开这个演讲的第二部分。
